title: Shift-in preserves concatenation
statement: Let $w$ assign a finite list of optional Boolean values to each of $\ell$ indices, and let the side word be the concatenation of these lists in index order. For any natural number $i$, shifting in leaves the side word unchanged: when $1\le i<\ell$ and the list at index $i-1$ is empty, the list at index $i$ is split after its first $2^{i-1}$ entries and those two pieces are placed at indices $i-1$ and $i$; in every other case the lists are unchanged.
